grade.first_issue: In Case 3, the assertion that obtaining a 90° angle allows Mulan to force every smaller θ is unsupported and false. The claims that she can force 2θ merely because 2θ≤180° and can manipulate the maximum angle to a desired value do not follow. Since this produces an incorrect classification, Rule A applies.
grade.summary: The claimed answer 0°<θ≤90° is false; the correct values are θ=180°/n for integers n≥2. For example, θ=70° is included by the submission but is not winning. Starting from (35°,35°,110°), none of the angles is a positive integer multiple of 70°. Because 180° is not such a multiple, after every cut at least one child again has no angle that is a positive multiple of 70°, so Shan-Yu can retain that child forever and avoid 70°. The correct arguments for θ>90° and θ=90° constitute meaningful partial progress, meriting the Rule A ceiling of 2.
strengths: The invariant argument for θ>90° is essentially correct: from a triangle whose angles are all below θ, both children cannot simultaneously contain an angle at least θ.
The one-move construction for θ=90° is correct after labeling two acute angles as the base angles.

errors.description: The final classification includes invalid values such as θ=70°, so it is demonstrably incorrect and subject to Rule A.
The entire θ<90° sufficiency argument rests on false or unsupported central assertions about forcing 2θ or otherwise obtaining an arbitrary prescribed angle.
